subject: Action Required: SecureCheck Ltd Contract Sign-Off - 28 Days Overdue
body:
Marcus,

I am writing to formally notify you that the engagement contract with SecureCheck Ltd. for the Zero-Trust programme penetration testing workstream is now 28 days overdue for sign-off.

The contract was submitted to Procurement for approval on 10 July 2026 following completion of vendor selection and legal review of the standard CREST-accredited terms. To date, no signed contract has been returned and no formal approval or rejection has been communicated.

I must draw your urgent attention to the following critical dependencies:

- The penetration test (Task 305) requires a minimum of 4 weeks to complete once the contract is executed (3 weeks test execution + 1 week reporting).
- The GDPR compliance certification application (Task 306) cannot be submitted until the pen test report is received and all Critical and High findings are remediated.
- The ICO submission deadline is 18 September 2026.
- To meet this deadline, the contract must be signed no later than 14 August 2026.

As of today, 7 August, we have 7 days remaining before that hard deadline is missed. If the contract is not signed by 14 August, we will be unable to complete the penetration test before the GDPR certification deadline. The regulatory fine exposure for non-compliance is up to £2.3 million under UK GDPR enforcement guidelines, plus the reputational damage of a public ICO enforcement action.

This risk is now rated as HIGH probability / CRITICAL impact on the programme risk register (Risk 6001, 6002).

I am requesting an urgent response by 09:00 tomorrow (8 August) confirming:
1. The current status of the contract review
2. An exact date by which sign-off will be executed
3. Any outstanding issues blocking approval that I can assist in resolving

If I do not receive a satisfactory response by that time, I will be escalating this formally to the CEO and to the Board Risk Committee.

Regards,
Helen Watts
CISO | Programme Manager, Zero-Trust Cybersecurity Overhaul
Direct: +44 20 7946 0831

subject: ESCALATION: GDPR Compliance Deadline at Risk - Procurement Delay (PROG-GAMMA-2026)
body:
David,

I am formally escalating a critical risk to the Zero-Trust Cybersecurity Overhaul programme that requires your immediate intervention.

SITUATION SUMMARY
The engagement contract with our CREST-accredited penetration testing firm, SecureCheck Ltd., has been pending sign-off with Procurement (Marcus Reid, CPO) for 28 days. It was submitted on 10 July 2026. No approval has been received.

WHY THIS IS CRITICAL
Without a signed contract, the penetration test cannot begin. Without a completed penetration test report, we cannot submit our GDPR Article 32 compliance certification to the ICO. The ICO submission deadline is 18 September 2026 — a hard regulatory deadline.

The penetration test engagement requires a minimum of 4 weeks from contract execution. This means the contract must be signed by 14 August 2026 at the absolute latest. Today is 7 August. We have 7 days.

REGULATORY EXPOSURE
Failure to achieve GDPR certification by 18 September 2026 exposes the organisation to:
- Financial penalty: up to £2.3 million (4% of global annual turnover or £17.5M maximum, whichever is lower, under UK GDPR — our legal team has assessed this at approximately £2.3M based on our revenue profile)
- ICO formal enforcement notice — publicly listed on the ICO register
- Reputational damage, particularly given our data processing agreements with NHS Trust clients and Ministry of Defence subcontracts
- Potential contract termination clauses triggered in four client agreements

IMPACT ON PROGRAMME
The Zero-Trust programme is otherwise in good shape. Tasks 301 (Architecture Design) and 302 (IAM Implementation) are 100% complete. Task 303 (Network Segmentation) is 80% complete. The only critical path item now is the penetration test, blocked entirely by this procurement delay.

WHAT I NEED
I am requesting that you:
1. Contact Marcus Reid directly today to mandate contract sign-off by 11 August 2026 (to give us 3 days contingency against the 14 August deadline).
2. If sign-off cannot be achieved by 11 August, convene the Board Risk Committee for an emergency session to assess the regulatory exposure and consider alternative options (e.g., emergency procurement waiver).

I have already sent a formal written notice to Marcus this morning (copied to this email for reference). I am available for a call at any time today to discuss.

This risk cannot be absorbed at programme level. It requires executive action.

Regards,
Helen Watts
CISO | Programme Manager, Zero-Trust Cybersecurity Overhaul
Direct: +44 20 7946 0831

--- Forwarded: Email to marcus.reid@corp.com, 07 Aug 2026 08:30 ---

subject: RE: Action Required: SecureCheck Ltd Contract Sign-Off - 28 Days Overdue
body:
Helen,

Thank you for your email and I sincerely apologise for the delay in responding and in processing this contract. I fully understand the urgency and the compliance implications you have outlined.

To explain the situation from our side: the SecureCheck Ltd. contract was escalated to our external legal counsel for review on 16 July due to concerns raised by our in-house team around the liability cap clauses (specifically Clause 12.3, which limits SecureCheck's liability for data exposure during test activities to £500,000 — our standard vendor terms require a minimum of £2M for engagements involving personal data access). The external legal review has taken considerably longer than anticipated.

I received an update from our legal team this morning. They have agreed an amended Clause 12.3 with SecureCheck's legal representative, increasing the liability cap to £1.5M with a carve-out for wilful misconduct. This is not our standard position but is acceptable given the circumstances. The revised contract is being prepared for signature now.

I commit to signing the executed contract by close of business on 12 August 2026. I will ensure the signed document is sent to you and directly to SecureCheck Ltd.'s engagement manager by 17:00 on that date.

I understand this does not resolve the delay that has already occurred, and I take full responsibility for not communicating the hold more proactively. I should have flagged the legal review issue to you as programme manager at the point it arose in July.

If there is anything I can do to expedite from this point — including direct communication with SecureCheck to confirm the contract timeline — please let me know.

Apologies again for the very stressful situation this has caused.

Best regards,
Marcus Reid
Chief Procurement Officer
Direct: +44 20 7946 0422

subject: RE: GDPR Compliance - CEO Directive: SecureCheck Contract Sign-Off by 11 August
body:
Marcus, Helen,

I have reviewed Helen's escalation in full, including the risk register and the regulatory exposure analysis prepared by our legal team.

This is unacceptable. A £2.3 million regulatory fine, combined with the reputational damage to our NHS and MoD client relationships, is not a risk I am prepared to allow the organisation to carry when the resolution is a procurement contract signature.

Marcus — I note your response acknowledging the delay and committing to sign by 12 August. I am overriding that timeline.

CEO DIRECTIVE — MANDATORY COMPLIANCE

1. The SecureCheck Ltd. engagement contract must be fully executed and delivered to both SecureCheck Ltd. and to Helen Watts by close of business on MONDAY, 11 AUGUST 2026. This is not negotiable.

2. If any outstanding legal or commercial issues are preventing signature by that date, you are to escalate those issues to me directly, today, so that they can be resolved at CEO level. Do not allow legal review processes to run beyond their expected timelines without escalating.

3. Helen — please confirm directly with SecureCheck Ltd. today that they are ready to mobilise immediately upon contract execution. I want pen test activities to begin no later than 13 August.

4. Marcus — following resolution of this matter, I am asking you to conduct a review of our procurement approval SLAs for programme-critical vendor contracts and to bring recommendations to me and the Executive Committee within 30 days.

5. If the contract is not signed by 17:00 on 11 August, I will be convening an emergency Board Risk Committee session that morning to discuss regulatory exposure and to consider whether this matter should be disclosed proactively to the ICO. I will also be initiating a formal review of the procurement function's governance processes.

I expect confirmation from both of you once the contract has been executed.

David Thornton
Chief Executive Officer
Direct: +44 20 7946 0100

subject: Pen Test Readiness Assessment - Systems Ready, Awaiting Contract Only
body:
Helen,

As requested at last week's programme meeting, I have completed the technical readiness assessment for the SecureCheck Ltd. penetration test engagement. Summary below.

PEN TEST READINESS ASSESSMENT — ZERO-TRUST PROGRAMME (PROG-GAMMA-2026)
Assessment Date: 5 August 2026
Prepared by: Carlos Rivera, Lead Security Architect

IN-SCOPE SYSTEMS STATUS

1. External Attack Surface
   - All 14 externally facing IP addresses and 6 public DNS hostnames have been enumerated and shared with SecureCheck via the Statement of Work.
   - WAF rules have been configured to allow SecureCheck's test IP ranges (confirmed with their engagement manager, James Okafor).
   - Status: READY

2. Internal Network (Post-Segmentation)
   - Core data centre VLANs (18 of 21): Segmentation complete, test jump host provisioned in DMZ.
   - Legacy manufacturing VLANs (3 of 21): Segmentation 60% complete. I recommend these be included in scope but flagged to SecureCheck as partially segmented — findings in these zones should be weighted accordingly.
   - Status: READY (with caveat on 3 legacy VLANs)

3. IAM / Entra ID
   - 12 test accounts provisioned at varying privilege levels (Standard User, Helpdesk, IT Admin, Global Admin) for use by SecureCheck testers.
   - Conditional Access policies are live and will be active during testing.
   - Status: READY

4. Cloud Environment (Azure)
   - Reader-level access to the Azure subscription has been provisioned for SecureCheck's cloud assessment team.
   - Defender for Cloud recommendations baseline exported and shared.
   - Status: READY

5. SIEM / Logging
   - All log sources are ingesting into Sentinel. Test activities will be observable in near-real-time. I have agreed with Fatima that the SOC will maintain 'blue team observe-only' mode during the test — no blocking of SecureCheck IP ranges.
   - Status: READY

CONCLUSION
All technical prerequisites for the penetration test are in place. From a technical standpoint, SecureCheck Ltd. could begin the engagement the day after the contract is signed. The sole outstanding prerequisite is contract execution by Procurement.

I have confirmed with James Okafor at SecureCheck (via phone, 4 August) that their team is on standby and can mobilise within 24 hours of contract signature. They have held the provisional booking in their schedule through 15 August but cannot hold it beyond that date without a signed contract.

If the contract is not signed by 15 August, SecureCheck's next available slot is October — well past both the pen test completion target and the GDPR certification deadline.

Please use this report as evidence in your escalation to Marcus Reid.

Best,
Carlos Rivera
Lead Security Architect
Direct: +44 20 7946 0654
